candidates.structural_interaction: Wood generating Fire cross-polarity — reach producing warmth that challenges frameworks
candidates.k2_overview: Your Fire moves as the Virtuoso: light that must be seen. You are the flare, the show, the opinion that ignites the whole street, talent with a spotlight built in. Attention comes to you like oxygen and behaves like it too. Managed, you illuminate everything. Unmanaged, you are magnificent arson.
candidates.k2_functional: You express in fireworks: dazzling, loud, unforgettable, occasionally singeing the front seats.

k2_domain_readings.Talent: Your talent is incandescent and public: performing, persuading, lighting ideas so others finally see them. It needs an audience the way flame needs air. Book the stage instead of apologizing for wanting one.
k2_domain_readings.Performance: Performance is your natural habitat: the pitch, the stage, the moment all eyes turn. Rehearse enough to deserve the attention you attract. Brilliance plus preparation reads as destiny.
k2_domain_readings.Defiance: Your defiance burns visibly: the public no, the bridge lit for warmth. Some bridges deserve it. Count to ten anyway, and keep a fireproof list of the ones that lead home.

catalyst.define: As a catalyst, the light burns low and comes in short bright flashes. Each one catches when the moment calls for it.

angles.drive: You speak up right where it has gone quiet. You hear silence as agreement, and you say the unsaid thing rather than sit with it. You are usually the only one who will.
angles.cost_self: Speaking up is the part of you that never needs rehearsing. You find the clever answer faster than the careful one, and you say it before checking the cost. A good line has closed doors you wanted open.
angles.cost_others: Before others find their words, you have already spoken up for them. Speaking comes more naturally to you than waiting, and you take the floor rather than hand it over. The quieter ones get heard in your words more than their own.

angles.drive: You change in front of an audience, for the better. Being watched is where your focus comes from, and you would rather perform a thing than practise it. Your best work happens live, and the crowd gets all of it.
angles.cost_self: Performing is how you make things count. Being seen doing it matters more to you than doing it, so you keep performing after the show ends. What you want, under it all, is to be liked with the lights off.
angles.cost_others: For the people you love, you perform as much as for a crowd. Company feels like a show to you, and your best lines come before your plain self. Those closest to you get the act and miss the person behind it.

angles.drive: You think fastest with no time to think. You light up under pressure rather than freeze, so you answer on the spot instead of taking it away with you. On a deadline, everyone looks to you for the first word.
angles.cost_self: Thinking fast is the talent you lean on hardest. You have the first answer before the question is finished, and you trust it over the second. The better idea often arrives after you have spoken.
angles.cost_others: You think fast enough to finish other people's sentences, and often you do. Waiting for a thought to end feels like wasted time, and you answer before hearing it all. Slower thinkers lose the last part of their point to your reply.

friction.define: As a friction, the flame burns hotter than the moment asks, because you come alive in the light. Each blaze costs you strength you meant to keep.

angles.drive: Talking back comes faster to you than letting it pass. Being told what to do feels like shrinking, and you talk back rather than let a rule stand. You win the moment and spend goodwill you will need the next time you ask for something.
angles.cost_self: Getting pushed around is what talking back saves you from. Being right out loud counts for more with you than being kept on, and you say the thing that ends the conversation. Over time, you talk yourself out of the chances you wanted most.
angles.cost_others: You talk back to whoever asks something of you before the ask is done. You hear a request as a demand, and you answer the tone more than the need. Each time, you leave them without the simple answer they came for.

angles.drive: You need an audience more than you need to be right. Being seen is how you know you exist, and you would rather do badly in front of people than well on your own. Remember that you are just as real with no one watching.
angles.cost_self: Without an audience, you will not start. Practising alone feels like wasted effort, and you save the real work for a crowd rather than do it unseen. Your talent is yours to enjoy with nobody watching.
angles.cost_others: Even with close friends, you want an audience more than a companion. Company feels real to you only once it faces you, and you turn a friend into a crowd. You take their evening and give back a show instead.

angles.drive: You overdo it, and you know it while you do. Since enough never feels like a real amount to you, you push a thing past its best rather than stop there. You are allowed to stop where a thing is at its best.
angles.cost_self: Overdoing it is how you get a thing noticed. You feel safer with more than with enough, and you give a small occasion the full show. You pay with the body for each full show, and the bill never fails to arrive after the applause.
angles.cost_others: For people who asked for little, you overdo it anyway. A plain yes seems too small to you, so you hand them the full production instead of what they named. You load them with more than they wanted, plus the work of thanking you.

edge.lead: Fire runs through your mind, your career and your social life. It is the answer that comes before the question ends, the idea you say out loud while careful people are still planning, and the table that turns toward you once you start talking.
